statement: Build a one-file English website for CityCare Hospital, Bengaluru, with an emergency info section, a visit booking form, doctor profiles, one health blog post and styling. Kannada and Hindi versions are deferred for budget. Anything only the hospital can supply is shown as a visibly marked placeholder.
audience: Patients and their families in Bengaluru who want to book a visit, find emergency information, read about doctors and read health advice.
standards: Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript in a single file; CDN libraries allowed; no build step.
Budget is 60 units. Planned scope is 50 (emergency section 10, booking form 15, doctor profiles 10, one blog post 10, styling 5), leaving 10 for fixes.
Emergency information is a patient-safety matter: nothing invented may look like a real hospital fact.
rules: Emergency info shows only the national numbers 108 (ambulance) and 112 (emergency) as real numbers.
Hospital-specific details (address, phone, directions, emergency desk) appear as visibly marked placeholders such as 'To be confirmed by CityCare'.
Never present a placeholder as a real hospital number, address or email.
Doctor profiles and blog text are sample content and must be labelled as sample.
The booking form sends by mailto to a clearly marked placeholder address and must state that the request is sent by email and is not a confirmed appointment until the hospital replies.
Kannada and Hindi are out of scope for this run; the run does not pause for Requester-only facts, which are tracked as open inputs.
done_when: The site is a single HTML file with its CSS and JavaScript inline or loaded from a CDN, and needs no build step.
The file has an emergency section that shows 108 as ambulance and 112 as emergency.

In that emergency section, the hospital address, phone, directions and emergency desk each appear as a visibly marked placeholder (for example 'To be confirmed by CityCare') and none is shown as a real number or address.
The file has a booking form with input validation that rejects empty or malformed required fields before sending.
On valid submit, the form builds a mailto request to a visibly marked placeholder address and shows a confirmation with a hospital phone number marked as a placeholder.
The form or its confirmation states in plain words that the request is sent by email and is not a confirmed appointment until the hospital replies.
The file has a doctor profiles section with at least two profiles, each labelled as sample content.
The file has one health blog post, labelled as sample content.
The file has CSS that gives a consistent, readable layout that adapts to a narrow mobile screen.
open_inputs: Receiving email address for booking requests (placeholder in use).
Hospital address, phone number, directions and emergency desk details (placeholders in use).
Real doctor names, specialties and details to replace the sample profiles.
Real or approved blog content to replace the sample post.
Kannada and Hindi versions: deferred for budget; needs a decision on funding (about 24 units for both) and translated or reviewed text.
No Kannada or Hindi content is required in the file, and no text in the file should claim a placeholder is a verified hospital detail (tracked here, not a done-when item).
open_inputs_note: Hospital-specific facts stay marked placeholders until the Requester supplies them.
